title: The Perfect Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Ines Eriksen has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidents, all tied to the wealthy parish of St. Aldwyn's and its founding family, the Vances. When a stranger's body is discovered dressed in clothes stolen from her own closet, Ines realizes someone is staging her into a fourth death — one designed to close the case forever. Following a ledger hidden in the parish's memorial plaques, she uncovers that the Vance inheritance was built on a forged will and a murdered heir whose memory was systematically erased. At the anniversary dinner, Ines exposes the patriarch's surviving daughter as both forger and killer; the final 'accident' was meant to be hers.
about_author: Bram Whitlock is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town church records before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep in plain sight, and lives within earshot of three different church bells.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Ines Eriksen records the finale of her podcast season, recapping the three 'accidental' deaths she quietly solved around St. Aldwyn's parish. Her POV establishes her obsession with memory — her mother's unsolved disappearance drives her. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by restlessness, because something about the Vance family still doesn't add up.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Police call Ines at dawn: a man found dead on the parish steps wears her scarf, her coat buttons, even her podcast lanyard. Detective Mara Quist, half-adversary, half-ally, lets her see the scene. POV alternates between Ines and Quist. Emotional beat: cold dread — someone has studied her closely enough to impersonate her death.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: The victim is identified as Daniel Okafor, a former parish sexton who once emailed Ines claiming he'd seen something the night of the first 'accident.' She never answered his email. Ines's POV, wracked with guilt. Emotional beat: the sickening realization that her silence may have cost him his life.

chapters.title: House of Vances
chapters.summary: Ines attends the Vance family's pre-anniversary reception under press credentials, meeting matriarch Eleanor, her son Julian, and daughter Rosalind. The house is a museum of curated memory. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: the uncanny politeness of people who know she's digging and want her to feel watched.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Ines lays out her evidence: each death benefited the Vance trust, each witness died or vanished, each inquest closed fast. Quist warns her off officially while slipping her an unofficial copy of Okafor's statement. Dual POV: Ines and Quist. Emotional beat: the thrill of confirmation colliding with fear of what confirming it invites.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Key
chapters.summary: Searching Okafor's rented room, Ines finds an old iron key tagged with a date — the night of the first death — and a torn photograph of a young woman no family album acknowledges. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve; the erased girl becomes her mission.

chapters.title: What the Plaques Say
chapters.summary: Ines notices the memorial plaques' donation amounts repeat in odd sequences — a cipher. Father Ambrose, the aging priest, deflects nervously but lets slip that the ledger room was re-keyed decades ago. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: the electric moment a hidden pattern reveals itself in plain sight.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Kindness
chapters.summary: Rosalind Vance befriends Ines over tea, offering archives access and disarming honesty about her family's cruelties. Ines can't tell if it's alliance or bait. Alternating POV: Ines and Rosalind, who privately burns a letter. Emotional beat: warmth with a hairline crack of menace running through it.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Quist identifies the photo: Margaret Vance, declared dead abroad in 1971, no body, no inquest. Her share of the inheritance dissolved into the trust. Ines realizes the 'accidents' began the year Margaret would have turned twenty-five. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: fury at how neatly a person can be deleted from a family's memory.

chapters.title: Anniversary Countdown
chapters.summary: The town prepares for the Vance tercentenary dinner; invitations arrive bearing Ines's name — she never RSVP'd. Someone wants her at that table. Julian confronts her, threatening litigation. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: claustrophobia tightening as the deadline becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Using Okafor's key, Ines enters the sealed ledger room beneath the vestry and finds the parish accounts — and penciled marginalia in Margaret's hand tracking money that never reached her. Footsteps above force her to hide. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: discovery and terror in the same breath.

chapters.title: Father Ambrose Confesses, Sort Of
chapters.summary: The priest admits he helped bury the scandal as a young curate: a forged will, a paid-off doctor, a girl shipped away pregnant. He swears he never knew she died. His guilt is real; his courage isn't. Alternating POV: Ambrose and Ines. Emotional beat: pity for a weak man who chose the institution over the truth.

chapters.title: Margaret Alive
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's coded payments, Ines traces a pension fund to a nursing home two counties over — where an elderly woman with Margaret's eyes receives anonymous checks. But when Ines arrives, the room is freshly emptied. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: hope snatched away, and the certainty that someone moved her first.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident, Drafted
chapters.summary: Quist shares forensics: Okafor was poisoned before he ever reached the steps, and the clothes were taken from Ines's dry cleaner — an inside job. The staging wasn't to frame her; it was to make her the story that dies with the case. Dual POV: Ines and Quist. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also the quarry.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Julian, drinking alone, reveals he's spent years suspecting his mother forged the will but lacked proof; he offers Ines the family's private papers. Rosalind watches them from the stairwell. Alternating POV: Julian and Rosalind. Emotional beat: fragile alliance forming inside a house where every alliance is transactional.

chapters.title: The Cipher Breaks
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing plaque donations with hymn numbers, Ines decodes the full ledger: every 'accident,' every payoff, and a final entry dated the coming anniversary — a disbursement labeled simply 'I.E.' Ines's POV. Emotional beat: ice-water clarity; her death has been budgeted like everything else.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Version
chapters.summary: Eleanor summons Ines and tells her own story: Margaret was reckless, the will was fair, the family survived because someone made hard choices. It's almost convincing — until Ines notices Eleanor quoting details only the forger could know. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: the vertigo of hearing evil narrated as duty.

chapters.title: Where They Kept Her
chapters.summary: Rosalind, cornered by Ines with the decoded ledger, breaks: it was her mother's operation, and Rosalind has been moving Margaret — still alive, silenced by decades of dependency — between facilities to protect herself. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: horror braided with unexpected compassion for a co-victim turned accomplice.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Ines walks into the tercentenary dinner wearing the clothes they stole from her closet, seat card and all. Toasts begin; Quist waits outside; Julian stalls the schedule. Ines's POV, taut and ceremonial. Emotional beat: walking calmly into the trap because the trap is also the stage.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: During the founder's toast, Ines stands and reads the ledger aloud, entry by entry, as Eleanor's composure fractures and Rosalind finally corroborates. Eleanor reaches for the wine — Ines stops her hand mid-air; the glass was for Ines. Climax. Alternating POV: Ines and Quist entering. Emotional beat: public truth as a held breath before the shatter.

chapters.title: Margaret's Testimony
chapters.summary: Margaret Vance, frail and lucid, gives her statement to Quist: the forged will, the threats, the decades of quiet captivity. The estate freezes; the trust dissolves; the plaques come down for forensic study. Alternating POV: Margaret and Ines. Emotional beat: restitution arriving too late to be sweet, but arriving.

chapters.title: What Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ines records a new season opener — not about the guilty, but about Margaret, restoring her name episode by episode. She answers an old email from another ignored witness. Final image: the empty ledger room, sunlight through the grate. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — memory kept is its own justice.
